title: Taking Control: Why Data Ownership and Digital Infrastructure are Game-Changers for CRE
excerpt: Unlock the potential of your CRE assets by controlling digital infrastructure and data.
content:
Understanding the Shift: Why Digital Infrastructure Matters

In the inaugural episode of the Peak Property Performance® Podcast, Bill Douglas and Drew Hall dive into a transformative concept for commercial real estate (CRE) owners: the importance of owning and controlling your data and digital infrastructure. It’s a shift from viewing these elements as mere utilities to recognizing them as strategic assets that can drive significant financial outcomes.

"If you don't own your data & digital infrastructure, your vendors do," Bill aptly noted during the episode. This episode sets the stage for a series dedicated to empowering property owners with actionable insights to reduce costs, increase net operating income (NOI), and future-proof their assets.

The Real Power of Data-Driven Decisions

Drew Hall emphasizes the substantial impact that data can have when properly harnessed. "The real power of harnessing all the information...and then doing something with it, making it actionable, like how much of a financial difference it can make in commercial real estate," Drew shared.

For many CRE owners, the challenge lies in accessing this data. Often, the data exists but is siloed within disparate systems or controlled by third-party vendors. By implementing the PPP 5C™ framework—Clarify, Connect, Collect, Coordinate, Control—owners can not only access but also leverage this data for strategic decision-making.

Beyond PropTech: Clarifying the Infrastructure Layer

Bill makes it clear that the discussion is not about PropTech. "PropTech is an industry in itself...but it’s going to use data," he explains. Instead, the focus is on the infrastructure layer that supports these technologies. This layer, often overlooked, is what owners must control to truly own their data.

Imagine a building where the connectivity user experience is controlled by the owner. This not only differentiates the property in a competitive market but also attracts technology-driven tenants willing to pay a premium.

Addressing Key Expense Drivers

A significant portion of the episode is dedicated to discussing how data and digital infrastructure can address the three major expense drivers in CRE: occupancy, insurance, and utilities.

  • Occupancy: By controlling the digital environment, owners can enhance tenant experiences, leading to higher occupancy rates.
  • Insurance: Detailed, real-time data can inform underwriters, often resulting in reduced premiums.
  • Utilities: Leveraging data to optimize energy use can lead to substantial cost savings, sometimes reducing expenses by up to 12% in the first year alone.

These strategies not only improve NOI but also create sustainable business practices.

Personal Insights and Industry Impact

Throughout the episode, both Bill and Drew share personal stories that shaped their understanding of the CRE landscape. Drew’s journey from aspiring chiropractor to tech architect underscores a fundamental belief: the power of connectivity to transform lives. "I ended up wanting to make things connect," Drew reflects, a philosophy that now drives OpticWise’s mission.

Bill’s experience, from the corporate world to tech entrepreneurship, highlights the potential of technology to solve big problems. "I like using technology to solve big problems," Bill explains, pointing to the scalability and impact of digital infrastructure solutions.

Actionable Takeaways for CRE Owners

The key takeaway from this episode is clear: CRE owners must take control of their digital infrastructure to unlock the full potential of their assets. Start by asking the pivotal questions: Who owns and controls your data flow? Who owns and controls your digital infrastructure?

The answers to these questions form the foundation for making data-driven decisions that can significantly enhance property performance. As Bill suggests, "Imagine what you could do...if you were able to look across disparate data sources within your property and within your portfolio."

For a deeper dive into these concepts, consider exploring the Peak Property Performance® Book here or listen to the full episode on the podcast page.
